label: early original-phase step (t=1-4), current token in {n,y,u,r,g,s} after an earlier t/g/0/2/y/z/c/e
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at early positions: 98% of activation mass falls on t=1-4, 87% on t=2-3. It never fires at t=0 or on the <DEL> step, and fires very little in the copy phase (1.7% of mass). Within that window it acts like a soft conjunction of the current token and earlier tokens. The current token is usually n, y, u, r, g or s (n gives 6.4x lift); earlier tokens are usually t, g, 0 or 2 (t as previous or first token gives about 6x lift). It mostly fires on the first occurrence of a token. The strongest activations (about 0.95 of max) are n or u at t=2-3 right after t t, t g or 0 t. The cue looks additive rather than a clean rule: a time window alone gives recall 0.97 but precision 0.03, and adding the token sets plateaus at dev F1 around 0.35-0.39 (mass recall 0.79). Many misses are other tokens such as k, i, j or q that follow t/0/2, and many false positives are the right tokens without a strong enough history.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: n, u, y, r; t=6: v, u, n; t=12: v, s, i) and the previous input (most: t, g, y, 2, 0, e; least: h, i, m, v); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, t=2, t=4.
